titre: Press Review: Shaykh Mohamed Faouzi al-Karkari in Chicago and Denver
corps:
Shaykh Mohamed Faouzi al-Karkari’s testimony about death and near-death experiences has been picked up by several American media outlets. During his stay in the United States, the Shaykh was invited to speak at the University of Chicago, and then in Denver at the annual meeting of the American Academy of Religion.

At the University of Chicago

On November 19, at the University of Chicago Divinity School, the Shaykh took part in a session titled “Sentenced to Life,” held as part of the course Witnessing the Afterlife: Anthropological and Islamic Approaches to Near-Death Experiences.

During the session, he shared three experiences in which he came face to face with death, and the spiritual lessons he drew from them. He explained in particular the Sufi understanding of the barzakh, as well as the distinction between a near-death experience and the spiritual practice of “voluntary death,” summed up in the Sufi tradition by the expression “dying before you die.”

His stay continued with several exchanges in Chicago on the muraqqaʿa, the symbolic garment of the Karkariya path, as well as an interfaith gathering devoted to the Divine Names and to the Christian and Muslim mystical traditions.

In Denver — American Academy of Religion

On November 21, the Shaykh took part in the annual meeting of the American Academy of Religion, in a roundtable on Islam, psychedelics and Muslim communities around the world. He offered in particular a reflection on states of consciousness and spiritual transformation, stressing the role of the remembrance of God, discipline and the inner journey.
